chunks: O believers, fasting is enjoined on you as it was on those before you, so that you might become righteous.
ai.seo_question: What is the purpose of fasting in Islam according to the Quran?
ai.summary: This foundational verse from Surah Al-Baqarah institutes the obligatory fast (sawm) for the Muslim Ummah, explicitly linking the practice to the traditions of earlier prophets to emphasize its continuity in divine law. Shia scholarship highlights that the ultimate objective is attaining taqwa (God-consciousness), a spiritual state where fasting serves as a practical mechanism for self-discipline and moral refinement, as further elaborated in the subsequent verses regarding the specific rulings and exemptions.
